Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: CITY OF EMMONAK
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 500 gallons
POWER PLANT OPERATORS WERE TRANFERRING FUEL BETWEEN TANKS TO MAKE ROOM IN PREPARATION FOR A SCHEDULED FUEL DELIVERY. THE PUMPED FUEL INTO A TANK THEY ASSUMED WAS EMPTY AND OVER FILLED THE TANK. THE OPERATORS WERE NOT CONTINUOUSLY MONITORING THE TANK BEING FILLED AND THE SPILL WAS NOT WITNESSED FOR APPROXIMATELY 15 MINUTES. NUMBER 1 ARCTIC GRADE DIESEL FUEL SPILLED OVER THE RIM OF THE TANK INTO A LINED SECONDARY CONTAINMENT DIKE. SOME FUEL SPLASHED OUTSIDE THE DIKED AREA AND A SHEEN WAS VISABLE ON A 7'X30' PUDDLE OF STANDING WATER.

Report DescriptionINITIAL INCIDENT TYPE: CLASS BRAVO MISHAP / PERSONNEL CASUALTY LOCATION: USCG TRAINING CENTER YORKTOWN, VIRGINIA TIME INCIDENT OCCURRED: 1000 ET / 1400 Z TIME OF INITIAL REPORT TO NCC: 1100 ET / 1500 Z NAME OF REPORTING UNIT: USCG TRAINING CENTER YORKTOWN AMPLIFYING INFORMATION: • USCG TRAINING CENTER YORKTOWN REPORTED A CLASS BRAVO MISHAP DUE TO AN EXPLOSION ON A USCG RESPONSE BOAT RESULTING IN FOUR MILD INJURIES AND ONE CRITICAL INJURY. • BM-A STUDENTS IN A TRAINING ENVIRONMENT WERE IN THE PROCESS OF CLEANING THE BILGE OF A USCG RESPONSE SMALL BOAT WHEN OIL/FUEL IGNITED, CAUSING AN EXPLOSION. THE CAUSE IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME. • FIVE BM-A SCHOOL STUDENTS WERE INJURED BY THE EXPLOSION. FOUR STUDENTS SUSTAINED MINOR INJURIES AND ONE STUDENT SUSTAINED SEVERE INJURIES. • THE SEVERELY INJURED STUDENT SUSTAINED 20% SECOND/THIRD DEGREE BURNS TO THEIR FACE AND UPPER BODY. THE STUDENT WAS MEDEVAC’D VIA LIFE FLIGHT TO NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL FOR HIGHER LEVEL OF CARE AND IS CONSCIOUS AND IN STABLE CONDITION. • DAMAGE TO THE USCG RESPONSE BOAT REMAINS UNKNOWN, THOUGH THE SMALL BOAT IS STILL AFLOAT. • THERE ARE CURRENTLY NO POLLUTION CONCERNS. • THERE IS NO REPORTED MEDIA ATTENTION. • NCC HAS STOOD DOWN THE CIC PROCESS, WITH CONCURRENCE FROM BOTH AREAS. ADDITIONAL DETAILS WILL BE REPORTED UP THE CHAIN OF COMMAND AND THROUGH DCMS WATCH.

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 40.998206, -76.439755 (Approximated from street_address)
Reported Spill Volume: 20 gallons
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** THE PROBE FOR A COOLING WATER TOWER MAKE-UP SYSTEM MALFUNCTIONED CAUSING ADDITIONAL MAKE-UP WATER TO BE ADDED TO THE SYSTEM WHEN IT WAS NOT NEEDED. THE OVERFLOW FROM THE COOLING WATER SYSTEM WAS PUMPED INTO A PIT PRIOR TO PUMPING TO THE WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT. THE PIT CONTAINED RESIDUAL SODIUM HYDROXIDE FROM THE DIE CLEANING CAUSTIC TANKS. THE PIT IS USED AS SECONDARY CONTAINMENT AND TO PUMP SPENT CAUSTIC TO THE WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT. THE RESIDUAL CAUSTIC CAUSED THE PH OF THE COOLING WATER TO ELEVATE INTO THE 12 - 13 RANGE. THE PIT OVERFLOWED AND APPROXIMATELY 20 GALLONS OF MATERIAL FLOWED OUTSIDE ONTO THE SOIL OF THE FACILITY.
